title: Nonplanar smooth limits of complex plane curves whose degree is a multiple of a largest Markov-triple entry
source_title: Smooth limits of plane curves of prime degree and Markov numbers
author: Kristin DeVleming; David Stapleton
difficulty_reason: Knowing that a weighted projective plane smooths to the plane does not extend the needed divisor class or guarantee a smooth member of its linear system on the partial smoothing. The authors control extension obstructions, compute the class/Picard and intersection scaling, and prove global generation and cohomology constancy for the relevant divisorial sheaves. Those new deformation and section-lifting results construct the smooth limit and its low-degree pencil before the standard gonality comparison, beyond merely applying the known Manetti surface classification.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Exact Theorem1.10 overC: a nontrivial positive Markov triple(a,b,c) in nondecreasing order and degree d>2 divisible byc. The author constructs a smooth projective nonplanar limit of a family of smooth degree-d plane curves; the prime-Markov assertion is one consequence within this claim. Read all new divisorial extension/class-group/basepoint-free machinery7–12 and consecutive pencil/gonality proof12–13. Hacking-Prokhorov independent Q-Gorenstein smoothing, Picard rank and classical gonality of a smooth plane curve are named prior foundations. Source13 final inequality prints c>ab-1 after explicitly establishing c>=2ab andab>1; those explicit preceding integer inequalities already supply the stated strict gonality gap. No degree5/7 classification, arbitrary-prime conjecture or higher-dimensional degeneration theorem claimed reviewed. PDF authors Kristin DeVleming and David Stapleton,11/2024/263/license verified.

historical_source_pdf_evidence.original_difficulty_reason: The authors extend Cartier divisors through partial Q-Gorenstein smoothings of weighted projective planes, control divisor class and intersection groups and produce a pencil with gonality below the plane-curve threshold. This deformation construction exceeds qualifying-exam algebraic geometry.
